profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 8, also called SUPERNAP 8, sits at 5225 West Capovilla Avenue, Las Vegas, Nevada, on Switch's Las Vegas "Core Campus" in unincorporated Clark County. Switch opened the building in April 2013, and its own press releases give 300,000 square feet in a February 2014 release and 350,000 square feet in an August 2014 release, a discrepancy this profile notes rather than resolves; both releases agree on 50 megawatts of power capacity. SUPERNAP 8 became the first multi-tenant data center in the world to earn Uptime Institute Tier IV Constructed Facility certification, awarded February 2014, followed by Tier IV Gold for Operational Sustainability in August 2014, real third-party Uptime Institute certifications rather than Switch's later self-created "Tier 5" branding. SUPERNAP 8 sits several hundred yards from Switch's original 2008-era Las Vegas 7 building, part of the same tightly built Core Campus cluster along South Decatur Boulevard, West Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road. Switch's Core Campus overall is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with Switch's Nevada tax-advantages materials describing a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement for customer equipment at Switch facilities, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development. Switch does not name a specific power utility on its Las Vegas campus pages, though NV Energy is the incumbent utility across Clark County as a matter of public record.

Switch has since built a large solar and battery-storage generation program, including the Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects and the more recent Gigawatt Nevada development, to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy claim across its Nevada campuses. Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus of which SUPERNAP 8 remains one of the largest and most heavily publicized single buildings, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs.

sources.title: Switch Press Release, SUPERNAP 8 Earns Tier IV Gold Status

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 8, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 8 at 5225 W Capovilla Avenue, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from datacenterHawk, a single aggregator directory, not independently corroborated by a second source this session.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 8 is a 50-megawatt facility opened in 2013 at 5225 West Capovilla Avenue on Switch's Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 50 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 1,250 racks. The building spans 350,000 square feet and earned Uptime Institute Tier IV Constructed Facility certification in February 2014 and Tier IV Gold for Operational Sustainability in August 2014. It qualifies the campus to host mission-critical multi-tenant workloads requiring sustained availability and renewable energy compliance.

Within Nevada's published data center capacity, Las Vegas 8 ranks third by announced power, behind two other facilities in the state. Nevada has 26 mapped data center sites but only 2 publish power figures, totaling 10.37 megawatts across both. Las Vegas 8 alone represents 48 percent of Nevada's published IT capacity, reflecting the concentration of the state's data center presence in Clark County's Switch Core Campus cluster. The facility sits several hundred yards from Switch's older Las Vegas 7 building as part of a tightly built campus that Switch markets as offering up to 495 megawatts total power upon completion.

Switch operates renewable generation infrastructure including solar and battery storage projects to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy commitment across Nevada campuses, though the specific power utility and grid interconnection for Las Vegas 8 are not published. The Core Campus has anchored Las Vegas as a secondary U.S. data center market, though the operator's tax abatement materials and renewable energy strategy are corporate governance claims not independently verified by third-party grid or emissions reporting. Whether the 50-megawatt figure represents total facility power or IT load only is not clarified in Switch's public specifications for this building.
